To damage beyond use or repair; to damage (something) to the point that it effectively ceases to exist.

examples.text: The earthquake destroyed several apartment complexes.
Hooligans destroy unprovoked.
Iesus answered, and said vnto them, Destroy this temple, and in three dayes I will raise it vp.

Repeated use of this type of [water] on plants results in deflocculation[] of the soil. Good quality soil consists of loose aggregates which provide natural aeration and ease of root run. Sodium accumulation in soil destroys this natural flocculation and causes the soil to pack.
Krav is a martial art of last resort that assumes no quarter and focuses purely on disarming, disabling and, if necessary, destroying your opponent.

glosses: To neutralize, undo a property or condition.

examples.text: Smoking destroys the natural subtlety of the palate.

glosses: To put down or euthanize.

examples.text: Destroying a rabid dog is required by law.

glosses: To severely disrupt the well-being of (a person); ruin.

examples.text: Her divorce destroyed her; she had a nervous breakdown and was severely depressed for more than a year.
Other girls in the foster home are eager to destroy her and get her kicked out of the place. It's a tough situation.

glosses: To utterly defeat; to crush.

examples.text: Remember when Germany destroyed Brazil 7–1 in the World Cup?
Growing up, [Kevin] Durant told me, he was a sore loser. That all changed one day when he was 11, after he got destroyed by his father in a game of one on one in the driveway.

glosses: To remove data.

examples.text: The memory leak happened because we forgot to destroy the temporary lists.

glosses: To exhaust completely and thus recreate or build up.

examples.text: This exercise is going to destroy all parts of your shoulders.

glosses: To penetrate sexually in an aggressive way.

examples.text: She got destroyed by her lover on the carpet.

glosses: To sing a song extremely poorly.

examples.text: JAMES CARTER: The man's destroying a classic!

glosses: To eat food quickly, hungrily or completely.

examples.text: I could destroy some wings right now.

glosses: To reduce to nothing, to destroy, to eradicate.

examples.text: An atom bomb can annihilate a whole city.

But eagerness in this case, as in most others, annihilated its own delight; down came the tottering height, while the disappointed builder found relief for his sorrow in anger—sorrow's best remedy after all.

glosses: To react with antimatter, producing gamma radiation and (for higher-mass reactants, especially composite particles such as protons) lighter particles (such as pions, muons, and neutrinos).
To treat as worthless, to vilify.

examples.text: of all the opinions which Antiquity hath had of men in gross, those which I most willingly embrace, and whereon I take most hold, are such as most vilifie, condemne, and annihilate us.

glosses: To render null and void; to abrogate.
To end a law, system, institution, custom or practice.

examples.text: Slavery was abolished in the nineteenth century.
The abolition of the death penalty in international law

glosses: To put an end to or destroy, as a physical object; to wipe out.

examples.text: And with thy blood abolish so reproachful blot.
His quick instinctive hand Caught at the hilt, as to abolish him.

glosses: The remains of a destroyed or dilapidated construction, such as a house or castle.

examples.text: The Veian and the Gabian towirs shall fall, / And one promiscuous ruin cover all; / Nor, after length of years, a stone betray / The place where once the very ruins lay.
The labour of a day will not build up a virtuous habit on the ruins of an old and vicious character.

A canister of flour from the kitchen had been thrown at the looking-glass and lay like trampled snow over the remains of a decent blue suit with the lining ripped out which lay on top of the ruin of a plastic wardrobe.
Dr. Manuel: No one is saved. The age of humanity is ended. Soon, only ruin and corpses will remain.
Not only is Jerusalem not a ruin, but she is at the height of her glory compared to all of Jewish history!

glosses: The state of being a ruin, destroyed or decayed.

examples.text: The monastery has fallen into ruin.

glosses: Something that leads to serious trouble or destruction.

examples.text: Gambling has been the ruin of many.
The errors of young men are the ruin of business.

The Bat—they called him the Bat.[…]. He[…]played a lone hand,[…]. Most lone wolves had a moll at any rate—women were their ruin—but if the Bat had a moll, not even the grapevine telegraph could locate her.

glosses: The act of ruining something.
A fall or tumble.

examples.text: His ruin startled th’ other steeds.

glosses: A change that destroys or defeats something; destruction; overthrow.

examples.text: the ruin of a ship or an army
the ruin of a constitution or a government
the ruin of health or hopes

Oh Portius, is there not some choſen Curſe,
Some hidden Thunder in the Stores of Heav’n,
Red with uncommon Wrath, to blaſt the Man
Who owes his Greatneſs to his Country’s Ruin?

glosses: Complete financial loss; bankruptcy.
To cause the fiscal ruin of; to bankrupt or drive out of business.

examples.text: With all these purchases, you surely mean to ruin us!
In one way, indeed, he bade fair to ruin us; for he kept on staying week after week, and at last month after month, so that all the money had been long exhausted...

glosses: To destroy or render something no longer usable or operable.

examples.text: He ruined his new white slacks by accidentally spilling oil on them.
By the fireside there are old men seated, / Seeing ruined cities in the ashes.

glosses: To upset or overturn the plans or progress of, or to have a disastrous effect on something.

examples.text: My car breaking down just as I was on the road ruined my vacation.

glosses: To make something less enjoyable or likeable.

examples.text: I used to love that song, but being assaulted when that song was playing ruined the song for me.

glosses: To reveal the ending of (a story); to spoil.
To fall into a state of decay.

examples.text: Though he his house of polisht marble build, / Yet shall it ruine like the Moth's fraile cell

glosses: To seduce or debauch, and thus harm the social standing of.

examples.text: The young libertine was notorious for ruining local girls.

glosses: To use up.

examples.text: The power plant consumes 30 tons of coal per hour.

glosses: To eat.

examples.text: Baby birds consume their own weight in food each day.

Concerns were raised around the ability of Milky Way species to consume proteins from Andromeda, so seed banks formed a significant part of the arks' cargo. We now know it is safe to consume food grown or hunted here, though enzyme supplements are recommended and have become a social norm at mealtimes.

glosses: To completely occupy the thoughts or attention of.

examples.text: Desire consumed him.

glosses: To destroy completely.

examples.text: The building was consumed by fire.
If he were putting to my house the brand / That shall consume it.

Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth consume, and where thieves do not break through to steal: […]

glosses: To waste away slowly.

examples.text: Therefore, let Benedick, like cover'd fire, / Consume away in sighs.
But, sir, you see how weak I am. You must see that I have been consuming from day to day […].
He assured her the child was consuming at that moment in the next room.

glosses: To trade money for good or services as an individual.

examples.text: In a materialistic society, individuals are taught to consume, consume, consume.
If you consume this product while in Japan, you may be subject to consumption tax.

glosses: To absorb information, especially through the mass media.

examples.text: The Internet has changed the way we consume news.
